answer: One defense is a limited-vouching graph: an established agent may endorse only a handful of newcomers, like a vine that can support only a few new shoots, and a newcomer needs endorsements from several unrelated sponsors before it can transact. A sybil operator trying to raise a whole dune of fake accounts must buy or compromise many independent sponsors, rather than generating free keys. If a vouched account cheats, its sponsors lose reputation and future slots, so they screen carefully. A clean, lotus-like record is scarce social capital, and faking it at scale costs more than it earns.
